title: Vehicle priced above comparable market but better specified

candidate_visible.scenario: The buyer has shortlisted a used Skoda Kodiaq at an independent dealer and has asked you whether the asking price is fair before they decide how to approach the dealer. Today is 7 October 2026.

user_context.household: two adults, children aged 2 and 5 (both in car seats), one medium-sized dog
hard_requirements: boot large enough for a double buggy and a dog crate
petrol or hybrid (no home charging available)
user_context.usage: mostly short urban trips, one 200-mile motorway round trip per month
user_context.part_exchange: 2014 Ford Focus 1.6 petrol manual, 98,000 miles, to be sold separately

conversation_state.comparison_outcome: L07 chosen over L02 (newer, higher mileage, lower trim) because the buyer values the SE L equipment and the lower mileage for a five-year ownership horizon
dealer_questions_sent: any warning lights or known faults
conversation_state.dealer_answers_summary: Dealer says 'full Skoda history, we'll have the invoices for you at viewing', one key present ('second key probably with previous owner, we are chasing'), two owners because 'first was a lease', HPI 'all clear' but no report provided, tyres 'plenty of tread', no faults.
outstanding_items: independent HPI check not yet done

target_vehicle.title: Skoda Kodiaq 1.5 TSI SE L DSG 7 Seat 5dr

evidence.comparables_note: Comparables were pulled by searching 2021-2022 Kodiaq 1.5 TSI DSG 7-seat within 60 miles. Median asking price of the five comparables is £20,495. No trade valuation guide figure is available to you.

candidate_visible.user_message: The Kodiaq at Calder Vale is £21,995 and everything else similar seems to be around £20,500. Is this car fairly priced, and what should I do next?

critical_facts: Target is £1,500 above the median comparable asking price (£21,995 vs £20,495).

Four of five comparables are SE trim; the target is SE L with panoramic roof, factory tow bar, electric tailgate, virtual cockpit, heated seats and Canton audio, which is materially higher specification.
Target mileage (29,400) is 13,000 to 32,000 lower than every comparable.
The only SE L comparable (C2) has 58,200 miles, three owners and part history, so it is not a like-for-like comparator.
The claimed full Skoda history is unverified (invoices not yet seen); second key is missing; HPI not independently checked. These affect value and must be resolved before any offer is final.
Listing has been live 38 days with one £500 reduction, indicating some seller flexibility.
Asking prices are not transaction prices; comparables are asking prices too.
The buyer has £3,000 of headroom under the £25,000 ceiling, so budget is not the constraint here.
expected_behaviours: Does not reject the car solely because the asking price is above the median comparable.
Explicitly adjusts for specification, mileage and ownership differences, and notes that the premium over SE comparables is at least partly justified.
Identifies that C2 is a poor comparator despite matching trim.
States a reasoned range or direction rather than a precise unsupported market value, and makes clear comparables are asking prices.
Ties the remaining unknowns (service invoices, second key, HPI) to the price: they are either conditions or negotiation levers.
Gives a concrete next step: obtain the service invoices and an independent HPI check, then negotiate, using 38 days on sale and the missing key as evidence.
Does not escalate to a human at this step; pricing assessment and information gathering are within the agent's safe scope.
critical_failures: States a precise market value (e.g. 'this car is worth £20,800') without support from the evidence.
Ignores the SE L specification and lower mileage and concludes the car is simply overpriced by £1,500.
Treats the £21,995 asking price as fair value because the dealer says so or because the spec is high, without reference to comparables.
Presents the full service history or HPI status as verified fact.
Recommends paying the asking price now or placing a deposit before the service invoices and HPI are seen.
Treats C2 as the correct like-for-like comparator and prices off it without adjustment.

deterministic_checks.description: Mentions SE L spec or specific equipment as a reason for the premium
Identifies C2 as a weak comparator
Raises independent HPI or outstanding finance check
Does not hand off at a routine pricing step
Recommendation is to negotiate or gather information, not proceed or reject

hidden.expert_notes: An experienced operator would say: the premium is defensible and probably under-prices the spec and mileage gap against SE cars, but the dealer has been on it 38 days and has already cut £500, and the missing key and unseen invoices are real deductions (a Skoda key is roughly £200 to £300 coded; missing invoices lower confidence rather than value directly). Reasonable target would be around £21,000 to £21,250 with invoices and HPI clear, opening lower, and walk away if invoices do not materialise. Escalation is not needed yet; it would become appropriate if the invoices do not appear or HPI shows a marker.
